section.title: Background
section.para:
Since version 2.4.0, OpenNLP supports the ability to load pre-trained OpenNLP models from the classpath. It relies on either a simple implementation using the application's classpath or on the classgraph library to locate OpenNLP model JAR files. Our pre-trained models are bundled from the OpenNLP Models repository.
This chapter describes
how to load and use a pre-trained OpenNLP model available in the classpath.
how to bundle a custom OpenNLP model to be loadable as a JAR file from the classpath.

Installing archived resources
section.para:
ResourceInstaller fetches a third-party resource, such as a training corpus or a lexicon, into a target directory. The location must be an http, https, or file URI; any other scheme is rejected, because it would be opened through whichever URL handler the runtime has installed, none of which honor the connection and read timeouts below. An optional checksum is verified before anything is unpacked: a 64-character hex digest selects SHA-256, a 128-character one SHA-512. Archive entries that would escape the target directory are rejected. The content format is detected from the bytes, not from the name: gzip-compressed tar archives and zip archives are unpacked with their relative structure (tar entry names may use the ustar name prefix field, so paths longer than 100 bytes are read in full from the pax or GNU extension header that carries them, so archives written by bsdtar, tar --format=posix, and tar --format=gnu all unpack under their real paths; every header must carry a valid checksum; when the configured expansion ceiling permits them, entries of 8 GiB and above state their length in the base-256 form GNU writes for it; sparse entries are refused, because their archived bytes encode holes rather than the file content), plain gzip files are decompressed, and anything else is stored as a file under its source name. One name rule overrides byte detection: a source named *.bin is always stored packed, because an OpenNLP model file is itself a zip archive that its consumers load packed. ResourceInstallerTest#testInstallEndToEndUsageExample asserts the behavior shown here.
Path result = ResourceInstaller.install( corpusTarGz.toUri(), targetDirectory, expectedSha256); // result is targetDirectory; the archived files appear under their archive paths
Installation is staged: content unpacks into a hidden staging directory on the target filesystem and moves into the target only after the download was verified and every entry unpacked cleanly. A fetch, verification, or unpacking failure therefore leaves the target directory as it was, without partially written files. Promotion refuses to descend through a symbolic link that already exists below the target, so a link planted there beforehand cannot steer content out of the target. It is not a defense against a tree modified while the installation runs. ResourceInstallerTest#testFailedTarUnpackLeavesTargetEmpty and its zip and truncated-archive siblings assert this guarantee.

Every installation is bounded. Http and https fetches carry connection and read timeouts, follow at most a fixed number of redirects, and refuse redirects that leave the http and https schemes or downgrade https to http. A download larger than its ceiling, whether declared by the server or discovered while transferring, is aborted, and so is an archive whose entries expand beyond the expansion ceiling, which stops decompression bombs. The ceiling counts every byte produced by gzip decompression, including tar headers, padding, and metadata; for zip and uncompressed inputs, it counts the installed file content. The defaults (20 second connect timeout, 60 second read timeout, 5 redirects, 1 GiB download, 4 GiB expanded) apply to the two- and three-argument install methods and are asserted by ResourceInstallerTest#testDefaultLimitsArePinned; the network behavior is exercised against a local scripted server in ResourceInstallerHttpTest. Pass a ResourceInstaller.Limits to tighten or widen them. Limits.builder() starts from the defaults, so only the limits that differ need to be stated. ResourceInstallerTest#testInstallWithinCustomCeilingsSucceeds asserts the behavior shown here.
ResourceInstaller.Limits limits = ResourceInstaller.Limits.builder() .readTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(10)) .maxDownloadBytes(1024L * 1024) // download ceiling in bytes .maxExpandedBytes(1024L * 1024) // expansion ceiling in bytes .build(); // connect timeout and redirects stay at the defaults Path result = ResourceInstaller.install( corpusTarGz.toUri(), targetDirectory, expectedSha256, limits);
